motivation: The completed fresh OrthoBench control reproduces historical F1 but replaces six native ortholog pairs with six others. This is not evidence that the CPP optimization caused differences: neither control used it. Current multispecies search drains imap_unordered results into insertion-ordered dictionaries, and singleton assignment chooses the first equal-score winning cluster. Establish whether arrival order affects decisions before requiring full-pipeline output equivalence.
hypothesis: Reordering complete species-pair hit blocks, while preserving every hit and each block's internal order, can change singleton assignment at exact cross-cluster ties. RBNH graph construction is expected to remain invariant under this block-only permutation.
controls: Use the retained, completed OrthoBench control100 numeric checkpoint: 251378 genes, 12 species, 18486508 accepted directed hits. Validate the recorded manifest and all arrays. Compare original arrival order, lexicographically increasing species-pair block keys and decreasing block keys. No new HMM search, alignment, gene-tree inference, benchmark scoring or default changes.
execution: First reproduce the existing singleton helper's order dependence on a small explicit equal-score example. Then derive the initial RBNH graph from the complete real checkpoint under all three block orders; require exact edge equality. Run the existing initial Leiden step once with CPM 0.1, seed 4 and isolates retained. Apply unchanged singleton assignment to that same partition under each hit order. Report changed query-to-cluster assignments and affected gene IDs, edge counts and raw identities.
guards: Require a complete terminal baseline and expected full gene/hit universe. Require each observed species-pair block to be contiguous and unique before permuting. Preserve within-block row order and exact hit multiset. Do not attribute the historical pair differences to this mechanism without a separate traced comparison. Any graph difference, input mutation, malformed checkpoint or incomplete run must be explicit.
interpretation: A deterministic-order correctness diagnostic, not new biological accuracy evidence or a full-pipeline speed measurement. Any subsequent canonical ordering policy must remain opt-in and be evaluated separately from the kernel flag, with native output/metric comparisons and failed trials retained. Existing live QfO and Three Kingdoms runs remain untouched.
